key_insight: GEAR shows that image tokenizers work better when they are trained together with the generator they serve, instead of being frozen beforehand. By aligning tokenizer representations with what an autoregressive model can easily predict, it makes end-to-end image synthesis more effective.
problem_solved: Traditional visual generative pipelines use a two-stage setup: first train a tokenizer for reconstruction, then freeze it and train the generator separately. This decoupling can create token representations that are good for reconstruction but not ideal for generation.
method: Jointly trains a vector-quantized (VQ) tokenizer and an autoregressive (AR) generator in one end-to-end framework.
Uses representation alignment to guide the tokenizer toward features that are easier for the AR model to model.
Removes the mismatch caused by freezing the tokenizer before generator training.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, GEAR suggests a more unified recipe for building image generators that can improve efficiency and sample quality. It is especially relevant for teams working with token-based generative models, VQ-based compression, and autoregressive synthesis pipelines.

paper_title: GEAR: Guided End-to-End AutoRegression for Image Synthesis
paper_authors: Bin Lin, Zheyuan Liu, Chenguo Lin, Sixiang Chen, Yunyang Ge
